newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore PM says new Chile trade accord possible.
newsitem.headline: Singapore PM says new Chile trade accord possible.

text.p: A new trade accord between Singapore and Chile could result from a meeting with Chilean President Eduardo Frei, Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said on Friday.
Goh told reporters several ideas for new investment and trade opportunities between the two countries were discussed.

He said they had also talked about trade liberalisation in the context of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum and the World Trade Organisation (WTO) and both men agreed there was a need for "a faster pace" of APEC liberalisation.
Goh said Singapore and Chile shared similar views on international and trade issues and that joint stands in international forums could be made by both countries.
Frei said the meeting had been "a broad and comprehensive review of our bilateral agreements".
He said six agreements on science, academic, and corporate matters were due to be signed during his visit to Singapore.
Goh said the main idea generated by the morning meeting was to more effectively use each nation's position as the gateway to their respective regions.
"Together we can find ways to channel goods and people between our two gateways," he said.
Frei arrived in Singapore on Thursday and will leave for Manila to attend the APEC summit on Saturday.
